sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 13.10.2021 at about 5.30 p.m. Puttananjappa was riding TVS-XL bearing Reg. No.KA- 64-J-4933 near M.M.Palyam Village, Agali, Ananthapur,

Andhra Pradesh, at that time, a motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HG-9764 came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased, as a result of which, he lost control over his vehicle and turned suddenly and fell down and sustained severe injury and died on the spot.

Immediately after the accident, dead body was shifted to Agali Government Hospital, wherein post mortem was conducted and SCCH 5 petitioners have incurred a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and Rs.1,00,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
3. Prior to the accident, deceased Puttananjappa was hale and healthy, aged about 62 years, working as coolie, thereby earning Rs.15,000/- p.m.

Due to sudden and tragic death of the deceased,
petitioners are put to great hardship, mental agony and shock.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HG-9764 and Agali Police have registered a case in crime No.86/2021 for the offences punishable under Sec.304(A) of IPC.
The 1st Respondent being the R.C.Owner and 2nd Respondent being the insurer of the offending motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- to the petitioners.

sentences.text: In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1/owner has appeared and filed written statement by denying entire averments of the petition.

Respondent No.1 has submitted that, Agali Police have registered a false case against the rider of the Honda Dio bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-HG-9764 and the said vehicle having vehicle insurance with respondent No.2 vide policy No.33397/01100674/000/00 valid from 02.03.2020 to 02.03.2025, the said policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further he has got valid permit to the said vehicle and not violated any terms and conditions of the policy.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.

Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared before the tribunal through counsel and filed written statement by denying entire averments of the petition.
Further SCCH 5 submitted that, issuance of insurance policy to the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HG-9764 and liability to pay the compensation is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
He is entitled to take shelter available under Sec.147 and Sec.149(2) of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further denied age, occupation, income of the petitioner, occurrence of the accident.
Further submitted that, the rider of the said motor cycle did not possess valid and effective driving licence, thereby owner has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Compensation claimed by the petitioners is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Late. Puttananjappa, S/o.

Gangappa, aged about 62 years was died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 13.10.2020 at about 5.30 p.m. while deceased was riding on his motor cycle TVS XL bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-J-4933 near M.M.Palym Village, Agali, Ananthapur, Andhrapradesh, at that time, one motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HG- 9764 came and dashed against the deceased motor cycle,
as a result he lost his control and turned suddenly as a impact deceased fell down and died on the spot?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent ?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 /wife of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW-1, further one eyewitness by name Eswara is examined as PW-2 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 SCCH 5 and closed her evidence.

 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

9. Issue No.1:-
The petitioners inorder to prove their case, petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased is examined as PW-1 and in her chief-examination evidence SCCH 5 she has reiterated petition averments.

Though she has been elaborately cross-examined by the Respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of the PW-1.
10.
Further to substantiate their case, one eyewitness by name Eswara is examined as PW-2, who got exhibited copy of Aadhar Card marked as Ex.P.16.

Apart from the oral evidence, the PW-1 has got marked copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, translated copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of P.M. Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.5, translated copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.6, case diary is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.10 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.11.

On the other hand, the Assistant Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and furnished copy of policy marked as Ex.R.1.
Respondent No.1 has deposed his evidence as RW-2 and exhibited copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.R.2, copy of RC marked as Ex.R.3, copy of insurance marked as Ex.R.4 and copy of DL marked as Ex.R.5.
Further except oral evidence, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioners case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about causing of the death of Puttananjappa out of the accident held on 13.10.2021 at about 5.30 p.m. when he was riding the TVS-XL bearing Reg.
No.KA-64-J-4933 near M.M.Palyam Village, Agali, Ananthapur, Andhra Pradesh.
In the absence of iota of SCCH 5 evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
12. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HG-9764.

Under such circumstances, considering the said Bhagyamma vs Honnappa on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113755119/
4 evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.

sentences.text: Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Puttananjappa was aged about 62 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, petitioners have produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.12, wherein year of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 1960, the alleged accident was occurred in the year 2021.

Accordingly relying on copy of aadhar card SCCH 5 of the deceased, age of the deceased is considered about 61 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 7 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

14. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as coolie, thereby earning Rs.15,000/-
p.m. to prove the said facts, they have not exhibited any income proof documents.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.14,250/- p.m. so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 15. Further petitioner No.1 is wife and petitioner No.2 is daughter of the deceased Puttananjappa.

To SCCH 5 prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar cards of petitioner No.1 and 2 along with aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.12, copy of ration card marked as Ex.P.14 and copy of family card marked as Ex.P.15 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Puttananjappa, hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

16. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 2 to .3, then 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/3rd of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

17. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, there is no addition of the monthly income, if the SCCH 5 deceased was aged more than 60 years as future prospects.

Petitioner No.2 being the daughter of the deceased is entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards loss of parental consortium.

Further they are entitled for loss of estate of SCCH 5 Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.
20.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.8,68,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

22. Further during the course of arguments, the petitioner counsel Smt.NSR argued that, it is the case of SCCH 5 head on collusion and eyewitness is also examined in this case and prays to allow the petition.

Per contra, the counsel for R2 Sri.S.M. resisted the said arguments and argued that, the alleged accident was held in Andhra Pradesh and this court has no jurisdiction and age of the petitioners is also wrongly mentioned and there is no driving licence to rider of the vehicle, the said fact is admitted by the witness and prays to award compensation on principle of pay and recovery.

" MM Palya, Andhra Pradesh .
MM Palya
So as per the said admissions of PW-1 and PW-2, admittedly the alleged accident was held in Andhra Pradesh.
By relying catena of decisions, there is no bar to file claim petition under M.V.Act anywhere in India.
But admittedly, as per the charge sheet materials, that means, Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sec.304(A) of IPC and SCCH 5 Sec.180, 181 of M.V.Act.
In the said charge sheet, Investigation Officer has categorically admitted about non-having of driving licence to the offending vehicle driver.

So in the absence of non-having of the driving licence to the offending vehicle driver as argued by the respondent No.2 counsel,
principle of pay and recovery applies to the present case in hand.

26. As per the observations made and findings given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s. Swarna Singh and other reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531 and in case of Pappu and another V/s. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592,
this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to issue directions against respondent No.2/Insurance Company to satisfy the petitioners by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this SCCH 5 order with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and recover from the respondent No.1/owner through process of law.

::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.8,68,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakhs Sixty Eight Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order and recover from the respondent No.1 with due process of law.
SCCH 5 The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 90:10 in the award amount.
Bhagyamma vs Honnappa on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113755119/
7

The petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The petitioner No.2 is entitled to get release entire award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
